messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Dubois <s.dubois@globex.eu>, Kenji Sato <kenji.sato@apac-retail.co.jp>
Date: 2026-10-10T09:15:00Z
Subject: Post-call: model evals & multilingual quality checks (EU/APAC)

Hi Sophie / Kenji,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Summary of needs: multilingual NLU + generation across FR/DE/ES (EU) and JA/KO/EN variants (APAC), with strict PII handling and near-production latency targets for inference.
- Recommended initial approach: run a focused eval over your 1k sample prompts per locale using two model families (one medium-sized quantized model + one larger accuracy-oriented model) so we can trade off cost vs quality.
- Deliverables: evaluation matrices (accuracy / hallucination / latency), prompt set suggestions per locale, and quick wins for prompt tuning or light fine-tuning if needed.

Could you confirm the priority languages and any compliance constraints (e.g., data residency for EU)? If you’re good with that, I’ll loop in our evaluation engineers and share a timeframe.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm priority locales & sample upload method (Drive or SFTP).
2) We run initial evals (3 business days) and share a summarized report + raw outputs.
3) Follow-up call to review results and agree on canary plan for a small production slice.

I attached a starter prompt set for review (prompt-set-eu-apac.xlsx).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the summary — that aligns with our internal view. Priority locales: FR, DE, ES for EU; JA and KO for APAC (EN is consolidated under our global team).

A couple of clarifications:
- Data residency: EU test data must remain in EU-hosted evaluation (we can share via Drive in the EU region).
- Evaluation goals: minimize hallucination on product descriptions and improve entity recognition for addresses/POIs in JA.
- Budget note: we prefer starting with a cost-conscious option first, but want to see accuracy numbers for a larger accuracy-oriented model as a comparison.

We’ll upload the sample sets to the Drive link you provided by EOD tomorrow. Can you confirm the two model names you plan to include in the comparison?

Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: model evals & multilingual quality checks (EU/APAC)

Thanks Marissa — we’ve got the request and will start the runs today. Plan below:

1) Ingest prompt-set-eu-apac.xlsx and validate sample counts per locale (will report any deficiencies).
2) Run parallel evals on EU cluster for FR/DE/ES and APAC cluster for JA/KO. Models: redwood-llama2-13b-q4 and starling-7b-intl as requested.
3) Add a third run with redwood-llama2-70b-fp16 (quality ceiling) for a subset (200 prompts) in JA to understand upper-bound for entity extraction.
4) Metrics: BLEU / ROUGE where applicable, entity-level F1 for NER, hallucination flags (model-generated facts not in source), and median latency (p50/p95).
5) ETA: initial CSV + one-pager by 2026-10-12 09:00Z.

We’ll attach raw diffs for the JA NER cases if we see regressions. If Sophie confirms sample upload to your Drive link, we’ll pick them up immediately.

Cheers,

Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: model evals & multilingual quality checks (EU/APAC)

Hi all — initial results attached (redwood-eval-summary-20261012.pdf) and raw diffs (japanese-ner-diffs.csv). High level:

- FR/DE/ES: redwood-llama2-13b-q4 performs well on generation metrics for product descriptions with a small increase in latency; starling-7b-intl improves factual accuracy by ~6-8% but costs ~2.5x tokens.
- JA (subset 200 + full run): we observed a regression in entity recall on Japanese address-like strings for the 13B quantized run vs the 70B ceiling run — looks like tokenization/multilingual pretraining gap. We flagged ~18 cases where NER recall dropped. See japanese-ner-diffs.csv for examples.
- KO: performance is comparable to JA on generative tests; entity recall slightly better than JA for the current prompt set.

Recommendations:
1) Prompt tuning for JA NER cases (we can provide 50-shot prompt templates) as a quick canary.
2) If Globex needs higher entity recall in JA, propose a canary using redwood-llama2-70b-fp16 for those flows (cost trade-off).
3) We will prepare a filtered prompt set for JA and run one more tuned pass — ETA for tuned pass: 48 hours.

Drive link to full outputs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-evals-Globex

Attachments: redwood-eval-summary-20261012.pdf, japanese-ner-diffs.csv

Thanks,
